title: Design a Distributed Cache
subtitle: From single-node LRU to Consistent Hashing, Replication, and Memcached/Redis clusters

stages.title: Stage 1 — In-Process LRU Cache
stages.bottleneck: Memory bounded by single process size; memory wasted as each app server duplicates the same cached items.
stages.narrative: **In-Process LRU Cache.** Uses a HashMap + Doubly Linked List inside the application memory footprint. Fast sub-microsecond access, but cannot share cached state across 50 API instances.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Modulo Sharded Centralized Cache
stages.bottleneck: Adding or removing a cache node invalidates almost 100% of keys (`hash(key) % N`), triggering a massive DB cache stampede.
stages.narrative:
**Modulo Routing (`key % N`).** Cache keys are routed to node `i` based on `hash(key) % N`.

**Catastrophic Flaw:** If Node 2 dies (`N` goes from 3 to 2), almost every key hashes to a different node. Cache hit rate drops to 0%!

stages.title: Stage 3 — Consistent Hashing Ring with Virtual Nodes
stages.bottleneck: Single hot key (e.g. viral post ID) overloads the specific cache node responsible for that hash ring sector.
stages.narrative:
**Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes.** Nodes and keys are mapped onto a 32-bit hash ring (`0 to 2^32 - 1`). When a node is added or removed, only `k/N` keys are remapped (`1/N` of total keys).

**Virtual Nodes:** Each physical node is mapped to 200+ positions on the ring to ensure even load distribution.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Master-Replica Failover & Read Sharding
stages.narrative: **Replicated High Availability Cache.** Primary nodes accept writes while read replicas handle high volume GET queries. Auto-failover via Sentinel promotes replicas if a primary crashes.
